nodes.text: connected areas devoted to cargo handling and storage

Build an industrial harbor loading dock centered on a clearly recognizable cargo-handling area. Use cranes for the principal vertical structures, with shipping-container groups defining the main storage masses. Include barrels, warehouse props, pallets, and warning signs as well. Arrange the containers into deliberate rows and compact groups to establish an organized industrial workplace, and maintain clearer gaps between the groups so that the loading area remains distinct from stored cargo.

Distribute smaller clusters of pallets and warehouse props near the containers and around the working area, indicating separate points for handling and storage. Beside some of these pallet groups and warehouse props, gather barrels; avoid spreading them evenly over the whole dock. Position warning signs along the edges of the working and storage areas, making their connection to cargo-handling activity visible.

Give visual priority to the cranes, containers, and loading space. Let the barrels, pallets, warehouse props, and warning signs provide the smaller details. Ensure that the complete arrangement is clearly identifiable as a harbor loading dock, with connected areas devoted to cargo handling and storage.
